Article Title: Bypoll results 2026: Ruling parties hold sway in Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Assam, and Puducherry
Article Text:
Bypoll results in Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Assam and Puducherry

Tamil Nadu: Vijay’s TVK expands its footprint

West Bengal: BJP’s march continues

Assam and Puducherry: Ruling parties hold ground

NEW DELHI: Ruling parties in their respective states continued to hold their ground as votes were counted in the bypolls on Friday, October 9. In Tamil Nadu, it was still “Thalapathy” Vijay and his TVK brigade making their presence felt. In West Bengal, the BJP strengthened its position, while in Assam, the saffron party maintained its comfortable lead. Puducherry, meanwhile, remained firmly with chief minister N Rangaswamy's ruling AINRC.Tamil Nadu and West Bengal went to bypolls in two assembly constituencies each, months after their assembly elections brought new parties to power in both states.Vijay’s TVK maintained comfortable leads in both Madurantakam and Dharapuram, seeking to expand its footprint in a state long dominated by Dravidian giants.TVK’s K Maragatham Kumaravel maintained a lead over DMK’s I Paranthamen in Madurantakam, while Sathyabama P was ahead of DMK’s Suganya in Dharapuram.Both constituencies had voted for the AIADMK in the previous Assembly elections, making TVK’s performance another sign of its growing electoral presence.The BJP, meanwhile, showed no signs of slowing down, maintaining huge leads in both Nandigram and Rejinagar.In Nandigram, BJP candidate Hasi Rani Rath was ahead of Congress’s Milan Pradhan in a constituency closely associated with chief minister Suvendu Adhikari’s political journey.Suvendu has won Nandigram in the last three consecutive assembly elections. In 2016, he was a close confidant of then-chief minister Mamata Banerjee. He later broke away from the TMC, joined the BJP and emerged as one of her fiercest political rivals.He has now succeeded former boss Mamata as chief minister of Bengal.In Rejinagar, BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar was also leading, keeping the contest competitive for the TMC candidate.The Bengal CM claimed that the BJP had secured around 60% of Muslim votes in Rejinagar and 80% in Nandigram, even as counting continued in both bypolls."Minority community found friend in BJP, voted for us in bypolls," Bengal CM Suvendu said after muslim-dominated Rejinagar supported the saffron party in big numbers.In Assam, the BJP appeared firmly placed in the contest for the Nagaon Lok Sabha seat, which fell vacant and went to a bypoll. BJP candidate Devasish Sharma was moving closer to victory as counting progressed.Puducherry, meanwhile, delivered a win for the ruling side, with chief minister N Rangaswamy’s party securing the Thattanchavady seat.
Article Summary: Vijay’s TVK brigade making their presence felt in Tamil Nadu. In West Bengal, the BJP strengthened its position, while in Assam, the saffron party maintained its comfortable lead. Puducherry, meanwhile, remained firmly with chief minister N Rangaswamy's ruling AINRC.

Article Title: Mary Kom’s ex-husband alleges character assassination, files defamation complaint
Article Text:
Olympic medallist Mary Kom’s former husband, Karong Onkholer

Olympic medallist Mary Kom’s former husband, Karong Onkholer, has filed a defamation complaint against the boxer before Delhi’s Saket Court, alleging that remarks she made during a televised interview damaged his reputation.The complaint was filed on October 6 and is pending before Judicial Magistrate First Class Shivam Gupta for pre-summoning evidence. The court is scheduled to hear the matter on November 19.According to the complaint, Onkholer and Kom married on March 12, 2005, and lived together in Faridabad. Their marriage was dissolved through customary practice on December 20, 2023, the complainant stated.Onkholer has alleged that Kom made defamatory remarks about him during a television interview aired on January 11, 2026, after the dissolution of their marriage. He claims the programme was broadcast to a nationwide audience running into millions.The complaint alleges that an ordinary viewer would interpret the statements, taken individually and collectively, as portraying Onkholer as “dishonest, unfaithful, unemployed, financially parasitic” and dependent on alcohol.It further alleges that the remarks suggested he had misappropriated money from Kom’s bank accounts and abandoned his responsibilities towards their children.The complainant has disputed the alleged portrayal of his professional life, stating that he sacrificed his own career and professional pursuits to support Kom’s boxing career before and during their marriage. The complaint says this account contradicts the alleged assertion that he had no career and had never been gainfully employed.Describing Kom as an internationally renowned boxing champion with a substantial public following, the complaint argues that the broadcast carried the potential to harm his standing as a spouse and parent.Onkholer has approached the court through advocates Akash Krishna and Pragati Sharma. The complaint invokes Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which deals with defamation.The allegations are part of a pending complaint and have not been established in court. The next hearing on November 19 is expected to determine the subsequent course of the proceedings as the court considers the matter at the pre-summoning evidence stage.
Article Summary: Olympic medallist Mary Kom’s former husband, Karong Onkholer, has filed a defamation complaint against the boxer. The complaint was filed on October 6 and is pending before Judicial Magistrate First Class Shivam Gupta for pre-summoning evidence. The court is scheduled to hear the matter on November 19.

Article Title: 'Complete stoppage of metro, rail services unacceptable': SC to Centre ahead of CJP October 10 Jantar Mantar protest
Article Text:
SC says restrictions cannot be reconsidered unless denial of permission for CJP protest is challenged.

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the Supreme Court should ease restrictions on protest movements? Yes, for the right to protest. No, public safety is paramount. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday raised concerns over the closure of Metro station entry gates ahead of the October 10 CJP protest in Delhi, saying the restrictions would affect thousands of commuters.The court pointed out that students, employees and senior citizens travelling from Gurugram, Greater Noida and other parts of Delhi-NCR would be among those affected."Everybody does not have a car… You cannot bring everything to a halt and leave people without any transport facility," Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said.The apex court also asked the Centre to ensure that train services to Delhi and metro operations are not completely suspended ahead of the October 10 protest."We make it clear that there shall be no complete prohibition on movement of metro trains," Supreme Court said.SC said services should continue in a regulated manner to minimise inconvenience to the public.The observations came as a team of senior advocates led by Kapil Sibal moved the Supreme Court against the cancellation of trains and proposed closure of Metro stations ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's ( CJP ) protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.During an earlier hearing, a bench led by CJI Surya Kant had questioned why the protesters had not challenged Delhi Police's decision to deny permission for the demonstration at Jantar Mantar.The court observed that it could not consider easing the restrictions unless the denial of permission was challenged."If there is no permission for protests, it will be an unlawful protest," Justice Joymalya Bagchi observed.Sibal, appearing for CPM MP M A Baby, argued that every citizen had the right to protest, even spontaneously.The Supreme Court said the right to peaceful protest at a designated place existed, but holding a demonstration without permission could expose protesters to prosecution.The bench also indicated that it could consider easing the restrictions if the organisers challenged the denial of permission and gave assurances about the gathering.The court said it could seek details about the number of people expected to attend, along with undertakings that protesters would remain peaceful and not carry weapons.Such assurances could allow the court to reconsider restrictions imposed over possible law and order concerns.Meanwhile, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned Delhi Police's decision to deny permission for the protest.He argued that Jantar Mantar was a designated protest site and police permission was not required to hold a demonstration there.Dipke also criticised the Centre over the cancellation of trains to Delhi ahead of Saturday's protest."Shut down entire country if you are scared of youth," he said, taking aim at the government over the restrictions.Delhi Police had earlier denied permission for the proposed protest, citing short notice, alleged violations during a previous demonstration and concerns over public safety, law and order and traffic management.Joint commissioner of police Nupur Prasad said the police had received an application from CJP co-convener Saurav Das seeking permission for a protest over the accountability of the Chief Election Commissioner."This intimation was considered, and it was found that the intimation was given in a very short span of time, whereas as per the prescribed guideline, the intimation has to be received 10 days prior to the protest that is planned," she said.Prasad also pointed to the party's conduct during an earlier protest at the same venue."Further, it is also important to mention that on an earlier occasion, when the Cockroach Janta Party was given permission to hold a protest there, they did not follow the lawful directions and did not follow their own undertakings given at that point in time," she said.She added that Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which allows preventive restrictions to maintain public order, was in force in the New Delhi area.Police warned that anyone violating the restrictions could face legal action.The restrictions come ahead of Saturday's planned CJP protest, with several trains to New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin cancelled and restrictions proposed at Metro stations.
Article Summary: SC says restrictions cannot be reconsidered unless denial of permission for CJP protest is challenged. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned Delhi Police's decision to deny permission for the protest. Dipke also criticised the Centre over the cancellation of trains to Delhi ahead of Saturday's protest.

Article Title: INDIA bloc protests against CEC: 'Unite to fight' proposes Uddhav's Sena; will AAP, DMK relent?
Article Text:
Both AAP and DMK have exited the INDIA bloc.

-

'A very critical request'

Will DMK, AAP join SIR protests?

'All parties should look at larger picture'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Should Arvind Kejriwal ’s AAP and MK Stalin ’s DMK join INDIA bloc’s fight against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over SIR? Well, the answer would surely be “yes”, as far as the allies of the bloc are concerned.Now to the more difficult question: Will Arvind Kejriwal’s AAP and MK Stalin’s DMK join INDIA bloc’s fight against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over SIR? Well, there is no straight answer to this one.The AAP and the DMK have a common enemy in the Congress . Uddhav Thackeray’s Shiv Sena (UBT) has now urged the two parties to set aside their differences with the grand-old-party to fight against "dictatorship". In an editorial in the party mouthpiece 'Saamana', Shiv Sena (UBT) said, “The entire country has been witnessing protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), but the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) have stayed away from it."The absence of both parties, who have officially withdrawn from the INDIA bloc, has highlighted the existing differences within the opposition camp on the strategy and format of the protest against irregularities in the SIR process.Former Congress leader and senior political commentator Sanjay Jha feels Shiv Sena (UBT)'s suggestion to both the DMK and the Aam Aadmi Party to join the INDIA bloc is a very practical, very reasonable, and at the moment, a very critical request."This is not about, at the moment, anything other than the fact that Indian democracy is in peril. It is unlikely that the CEC is going to resign of his own volition. It is pretty apparent that the government of Mr. Modi is going to be stubborn, and they will stonewall any effort by the opposition to demand and get accountability. Public protests don't seem to make any difference to the government. So the more the merrier," Sanjay Jha says.While the AAP has openly announced it will not be a part of the INDIA bloc’s protest and said “we are fighting this battle in our own way, the DMK has spoken in different tones.DMK spokesperson Saravanan Annadurai accused Rahul of adopting inconsistent positions on the electoral roll revision exercise and questioned why developments in Tamil Nadu had not received the same attention as the broader campaign against the Election Commission.In a post on X, Annadurai called on Rahul Gandhi to clarify his stand on allegations concerning names allegedly removed from Tamil Nadu’s electoral rolls during the SIR process.The DMK spokesperson also referred to a statement attributed to Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge that governments elected after the SIR exercise should be dissolved and sought clarification on why Rahul Gandhi had not publicly endorsed that position and whether such a stand would also apply to Tamil Nadu.Interestingly, a day later, DMK senior leader TKS Elangovan backed Rahul Gandhi on protests against the Election Commission (EC), saying that citizens have a right to protest against the government.“It is the right of citizens to fight against the government’s wrongdoings. That is what Rahul Gandhi did yesterday. Still, this government does not want him to protest because Gyanesh Kumar is being very useful to the BJP. Because of him, the BJP captured power in many states. In all these states, re-elections should be held,” Elangovan said.The DMK and the Congress had a very unpleasant parting of their two-decade-old ties after the 2026 assembly elections in Tamil Nadu, which the alliance lost to actor-politician C Joseph Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam TVK. While the TVK emerged as the single largest party, it fell short of a majority. The Congress rushed in to help Vijay not just form the government but also eventually join it. Making Congress a part of the government was something the DMK had resisted all along. The Congress move offended the DMK to no end. Since then, MK Stalin’s party has been unrelenting in its attacks on the Congress at all forums from Chennai to Delhi. The Congress, on its part, maintains that it kept the DMK in the loop while shifting loyalties to the TVK.The DMK is missing no opportunity to drive a wedge between the new allies. On Thursday, it lashed out at Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay-led TVK for not explicitly naming the BJP government over the arrest of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi after a protest in the national capital demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.Questioning the TVK's statement, Elangovan pointed out that it failed to identify the authorities responsible for the action against the leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha. "Who arrested Rahul Gandhi? They should condemn and explicitly mention the name of the BJP government," Elangovan told PTI videos.With the TVK establishing itself as the third pole of Tamil Nadu politics, at least for now, the Congress will have to choose one against the other, and to that extent its ties with the DMK will remain frosty for now. More so, after the TVK has officially joined the INDIA bloc. But the DMK’s measured criticism of the Congress-led INDIA bloc protests may offer a ray of hope to the opposition bloc allies of a future softening of stand by M K Stalin.Now, let’s turn to AAP. Here’s where untangling the strains in the ties may be very difficult, if not impossible. Relations between the Congress and the AAP have always been uneasy and tumultuous. AAP was initially a part of the INDIA bloc.However, ties between Kejriwal’s party and the Congress were never smooth given their competing political interests in several states. AAP attended the first three meetings of the INDIA bloc. The high point in their ties came in the run up to the 2024 Lok Sabha elections when the two parties agreed to a joint contest in Delhi, Haryana, Goa, Punjab and Gujarat.The alliance did not work and the ties ended for all practical purposes after the results were out. In July 2025, Kejriwal formally announced the end of ties.Uddhav Thackeray’s party has reminded Kejriwal of his bitter experiences with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and the Election Commission.“While Kejriwal was the chief minister of Delhi, he was put behind bars in a "false" case. Kejriwal's defeat was engineered by deleting names of voters from his constituency, it alleged. So, it is not in the AAP's interest to stay away from the INDIA bloc,” the Shiv Sena (UBT) wrote in its editorial.Sanjay Jha is confident that these parties will eventually join the opposition protest. He argues it is extremely crucial that the opposition includes everyone.“Whether there are any small, petty differences, whether there is any degree of discomfort with one or the other partner, everyone has to look at the larger picture. And the larger picture is that today people are out on the streets because they're concerned about the future of their vote and the future of democracy,” Sanjay Jha says.“And I believe it is very likely that the DMK and Arvind Kejriwal will join, because this is the time to put aside any petty squabbles and think of the larger goal of the country,” he adds.But this may be easier said than done. The Congress and the AAP are the main rivals in Punjab, where assembly elections are due early next year. The two parties are already engaged in a bitter war of words in Punjab, where AAP is defending its only government and the Congress is going all out to defeat Kejriwal’s party and reclaim its lost glory and government in the state.So, let’s see if this political compulsion decides the future course of ties between the two parties or the “larger goal of the country”?
Article Summary: Both AAP and DMK have exited the INDIA bloc. Uddhav Thackeray’s Shiv Sena (UBT) has urged the two parties to set aside their differences with the grand-old- party to fight against "dictatorship"

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc of opposition parties will be leading a delegation to meet President Droupadi Murmu, at 8pm today to brief her and submit a representation over the functioning of the Election Commission under CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the SIR process.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, TMC chairperson Mamata Banerjee, RJD national working president Tejashwi Yadav and general secretaries MA Baby (CPM) and D Raja (CPI) will be part of an over 10-member delegation of top leaders representing the various INDIA parties, sources said.It is learnt that the INDIA party MPs will be gathering at Central Hall of Parliament at 5pm where they will decide if they will march to Rashtrapati Bhawan for the 8 pm meeting.On the plan of INDIA parties to meet at Parliament ahead of the meeting with the President, TMC's Rajya Sabha MP Derek O' Brien said, "the Central hall is an apt place to meet as this is where the Constitution was born."This is day four of the ongoing agitation by the INDIA bloc where they resorted to street protests on the first two days and chose to visit Rajghat to pay their respects to Mahatma Gandhi in silence on Thursday.The decision to write to the President was taken at the INDIA bloc meeting on Sept 30. After that, the bloc wrote seeking time from the President for any day between October 7-9. It was conveyed by the President's secretariat that it would need to restrict their contingent of leaders to not more than 10. The INDIA bloc wrote back agreeing to the request.With the President agreeing to meet the Bloc leaders at 8pm today, the top leaders of the bloc were busy finalising the delegation to ensure the parties in the bloc are represented well.According to sources, Samajwadi Party Supremo Akhilesh Yadav is unlikely to be part of the delegation as he is caught up with unavoidable engagements, including his father Mulayam Singh Yadav's death anniversary on Saturday.However, SP is expected to be sending a representative for the meeting with the President, sources said. Whether Shiv Sena (UBT) and NCP(SP) will be sending representatives is still not known.Meanwhile, senior leaders in the bloc reiterated that the attempt was to bring together as many non NDA parties on the EC issue even if they are not part of the INDIA bloc.Biju Janata Dal (BJD) Rajya Sabha MPs Manas Mangaraj and Sulata Deo, along with former MP Muzibulla Khan had joined the INDIA bloc protest on October 6.On Friday, BRS working President KT Rama Rao (KTR) in a post on X said, "Nothing is greater than the Constitution of India. And no Indian citizen can be stripped of their right to vote.Gyanesh Kumar must go! No individual is above the institution. We the BRS party reiterate our demand that the Supreme Court needs to take suo moto cognisance of the irregularities in the SIR process and order an independent investigation headed by a sitting judge."Reflecting the opposition's mood to draw in more and more support on the EC issue, TMC's Derek O' Brien shared KTR's post saying, "Bravo".
Article Summary: The INDIA bloc of opposition parties will be leading a delegation to meet President of India Droupadi Murmu at 8pm today. The delegation will brief her and submit a representation over the functioning of the Election Commission under CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the SIR process.

Article Title: Mask and Face must face same consequences: SC stays HC bail, sends Rs 3,000 crore drug case accused to jail
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: “Mask must face the same consequences as the Face”, “If your masters are in jail, you will serve them better by being there, not outside” – were the caustic remarks by Supreme Court on Thursday as it send back to prison an accused who was granted bail by the Punjab and Haryana HC in a huge narcotic drug trafficking case.The case related to seizure of 5,000 tablets of tramadol from one Ashu Arora last February in Amritsar and subsequent unearthing of an inter-state illegal drug trafficking syndicate. Senior advocate Maninder Singh, appearing for the accused, argued that HC had granted bail six months ago putting a premium on the liberty of citizens and because of his illegal custody.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked, given the gravity of the crime, a Rs 3,000 crore illegal drug trafficking syndicate and seizure of 5,000 Tramadol tablets, can the illegal detention prior to arrest vitiate the arrest itself as has been cited by the HC?When Singh said that his client, Anuj Kumar Singh, was a mere employee of those who were allegedly running the inter-state drug trafficking network, the bench said, “You are a ‘mukhota’ (mask) which was as much involved in the crime as the face itself.”“When your masters are in jail, you can serve them better by being there with them, not outside,” the bench said while expressing serious concern over the menace of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances in the state. The senior advocate said that there was no evidence of any seizure of drugs from his client.The bench said, “In a game of football, there are 11 players but all of them do not have possession of the ball simultaneously.”The counsel said his client was not even a 12th player. Switching to cricket from football, the bench said, “He was either a cover or an extra-cover.”The bench said it would cancel the bail, ask the prosecution to complete the trial in one year and if it does not complete, then the accused can apply for regular bail. When Singh protested saying the accused had cooperated with the investigation and regularly attended trial while being on bail, the bench said, “For a Rs 3,000 crore drug trafficking case, one year in jail is nothing.”It asked the accused to surrender within two weeks and asked him to respond to the Union govt’s appeal against HC order granting bail.When Singh cited the HC’s decision to grant bail because of illegal custody prior to arrest and the premium it put on liberty, the bench said, “We also continuously ruled in favour of preserving liberty if there are other redeeming features. In your case, we do not find your cooperation in investigation or attendance of trial in the face of nature of crime and the restrictions in law to be a very relevant redeeming feature. Your arguments are most persuasive. In any other case we would have agreed with you.”
Article Summary: The case related to seizure of 5,000 tablets of tramadol from one Ashu Arora last February in Amritsar. Senior advocate Maninder Singh, appearing for the accused, argued that HC had granted bail six months ago putting a premium on liberty of citizens.

Article Title: Bengal bypolls: BJP surges further ahead in Nandigram; Congress trails in second place - top developments
Article Text:
Nandigram, Rejinagar results to indicate political mood after BJP's rise to power (Representative file photo)

NEW DELHI: BJP’s candidates maintained comfortable leads in Nandigram and Rejinagar as counting continued for the West Bengal assembly bypolls, with the Congress emerging as the runner-up in both constituencies.In Nandigram, BJP candidate Hasirani Rath was leading by 9,600 votes after the first round of counting, while Congress candidate Milan Pradhan was in second place. In Rejinagar, BJP candidate Sakharav Sarkar secured 11,614 votes after the second round, while Congress candidate Mohammad Abdullahil Kafi was trailing with 581 votes.Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) candidate Gulam Nabi Azad, son of party founder Humayun Kabir, had polled 446 votes in Rejinagar after the second round, according to trends shown by news channels. The Election Commission had not released official figures confirming the leads at the time of reporting.Counting began at 8 am amid tight security at the counting centres. The bypolls, held on Tuesday, are being watched as an early electoral test of West Bengal’s political landscape following the BJP’s victory in the Assembly elections earlier this year.Nandigram fell vacant after chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, who won both Nandigram and Bhabanipur in the assembly elections, retained Bhabanipur.The BJP fielded Hasirani Rath, the mother of Adhikari’s slain personal assistant, Chandranath Rath, who was shot dead on May 6, two days after the BJP’s election victory.Rejinagar became vacant after Humayun Kabir retained Naoda, where he had also won. His son, Gulam Nabi Azad, is contesting the bypoll on an AJUP ticket. The results from both seats are being closely watched for an early indication of the BJP’s electoral strength in the state and the opposition’s position amid divisions within the TMC.Nandigram holds political significance for both the BJP and the TMC. The constituency was central to the anti-land acquisition movement that helped bring the TMC to power in 2011. It was also where Suvendu Adhikari defeated Mamata Banerjee in the 2021 Assembly election. Adhikari, now chief minister, won the seat again in 2026 but retained Bhabanipur, necessitating the bypoll. The BJP fielded Hasirani Rath, whose son Chandranath Rath, a former aide of Adhikari, was shot dead on May 6, two days after the BJP won the Assembly elections.The contest in Nandigram has also been shaped by divisions within the TMC. The Mamata Banerjee-led faction’s nominee, Sanchita Pradhan Dey, withdrew after meeting Adhikari, following which Banerjee backed Congress candidate Milan Pradhan. A rival TMC faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee also contested the seat under a separate temporary party identity and the ‘envelope’ symbol. The result will indicate whether opposition cooperation can translate into votes and how the rival factions fare.More details awaited.
Article Summary: Nandigram fell vacant after chief minister Suvendu Adhikari retained Bhabanipur. Rejinagar became vacant after Humayun Kabir retained Naoda. The results from both seats are being closely watched for an early indication of the BJP’s electoral strength in the state.

Article Title: Sexual harassment case: Delhi court gives Brij Bhushan time to reply to acquittal challenge
Article Text:
Delhi court gives Brij Bhushan time to reply to challenge against acquittal

NEW DELHI: The Rouse Avenue Court in Delhi on Thursday granted BJP leader and former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh time to file a reply to a revision petition challenging his acquittal in a sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers. The court scheduled the next hearing for October 28.Women wrestlers have challenged the acquittal of Singh and former WFI secretary Vinod Tomar, who were cleared of the charges by a magistrate court on August 3. Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh had earlier issued notices to Singh and others on the appeal and sought their responses.The court has directed that the original affidavit and orders containing the names of the victims be placed in a sealed envelope. It also asked the appellant to submit a copy of the petition with the victims' names redacted.The case stems from allegations that Singh sexually harassed women wrestlers in India and abroad during his tenure as WFI chief. The allegations led to protests by women wrestlers at Jantar Mantar and an FIR registered by Delhi Police based on a complaint by a woman wrestler.Delhi Police filed a 1,500-page chargesheet against Singh and Tomar on June 15, 2023, following an investigation.The charges included offences under Sections 354, 354D, 354A, 506(1) and 109 of the Indian Penal Code.Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwani Panwar acquitted Singh and Tomar on August 3. The hearing was held in a closed courtroom.Advocate Rajiv Mohan, assisted by Rehan Khan and Rishabh Bhati, represented Singh, while senior advocate Rebecca John appeared for the victims and complainants.
Article Summary: Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh was acquitted of sexual harassment charges on August 3. Women wrestlers have challenged the acquittal of Singh and former WFI secretary Vinod Tomar. The case stems from allegations that Singh sexually harassed women wrestlers.

Article Title: 'How can you raise hands against children?' CJP sends message to police day before October 10 Delhi protest

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka on Friday issued a message to police personnel across the country ahead of the outfit’s planned protest at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar on Saturday, urging them not to use force against students and asking whether they wanted to be remembered in history as General Dyer or Mangal Pandey.In a post on X, Ranka alleged that police personnel were acting on orders from their superiors and questioned their role in the alleged nighttime detentions of students.“We know that whatever is being made you do at this time is happening on orders from above. But how can you raise your hands against our children like this? How can you take them away in the darkness of the night like common thugs?” he wrote in a message translated from Hindi.Ranka urged police personnel to reflect on whether their actions were consistent with their conscience and morality. Drawing a parallel with the British rule, he said some policemen had fired on their own countrymen while claiming they were merely following orders, adding that the nation continued to regard them as traitors.“The blood of July 20 is on the hands of the Delhi Police. Is that what you want too?” he said, referring to the July 20 violence.Ranka asserted that the protesters would reach Jantar Mantar on Saturday under all circumstances and continue their campaign, describing it as a historic battle to save the country.He ended his message by asking police personnel to consider how they wanted to be remembered in history, drawing a contrast between General Reginald Dyer, associated with the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, and Mangal Pandey, remembered for his role in the 1857 uprising against British rule.“The decision is yours—how do you want to be remembered in history: like General Dyer, or like the martyr Mangal Pandey?” Ranka said.Earlier, CJP official account shared a video claiming a group of students from Pune who were on its way to Delhi to join the 10 October protest, were detained."A group of students from Pune was on its way to Delhi to join the 10 October protest. They have been detained midway and are now being taken away in a bus to an unknown location," the post reads.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka on Friday issued a message to police personnel across the country ahead of the outfit’s planned protest. Article Title: AI use ups homework scores, but slashes exam marks: Study
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Evidence cited by World Bank suggests that unrestricted use of generative AI can improve what students submit as part of classwork while weakening what they actually learn - a warning with implications for countries such as India.World Development Report 2026 devotes a section to 'Generative AI and the Erosion of Knowledge, Learning, and Human Skills', cautioning that tools such as ChatGPT can reduce the mental effort through which reasoning, writing and knowledge are built.Its strongest evidence comes from China. A study covering students in classes VII-XII found self-reported AI use rising from almost zero to around 80% between 2022 and 2025. Six months after its first use, homework scores improved 18% even as students spe-nt less time on assignments, while monthly in-class examination scores fell 20%. Students who had ever used AI also scored, on average, 5-7% lower in senior high-school and college entrance exams.The report cautioned that the study had not yet been peer-reviewed and reflected the early phase of AI adoption.Gaurav Nayyar, who led the World Bank team that prepared the report, said the evidence points to both opportunity and risk in education."If students outsource the learning process to AI, then... that will be a problem," he told TOI.He said the evidence so far appeared more encouraging when AI was used by teachers rather than directly by students, pointing to its use in personalising and customising instructions to suit different learners.Other research reviewed by World Bank points in the same direction. Participants using large language models for research displayed lower cognitive effort and weaker reasoning, while studies found mental effort declining even when output quality improved. Students given unrestricted AI access also performed worse later when the technology was withdrawn.The report warns that if students use AI to complete homework, the "productive struggle" central to learning can disappear, potentially weakening foundational skills in reasoning and writing.But it does not argue against AI in education. A synthesis of experiments across China, Ghana, Nigeria, Turkiye and US found that 30 sessions of AI-powered tutoring produced learning gains equivalent to at least 0.5 years of schooling, particularly when AI complemented teachers and included safeguards against shortcuts. "AI can augment human capabilities," the report said, "but it must not replace the processes through which more advanced skills are acquired. "
Article Summary: World Development Report 2026 warns that tools such as ChatGPT can reduce the mental effort through which reasoning, writing and knowledge are built. strongest evidence comes from China. A study covering students in classes VII- XII found self-reported AI use rising from almost zero to around 80% between 2022 and 2025.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday orally remarked that its “forgiving nature” in commuting death sentences was contributing to an increase in crime, saying that there had to be a point where such leniency must “come to an end somewhere”.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu made the observations while hearing a plea seeking the premature release of a life convict whose death sentence had earlier been commuted to life imprisonment in a murder case.Justice Datta said that while murder convictions were earlier dealt with under the “rarest of rare” doctrine, “times have changed”. He questioned repeated instances of commuting death sentences and said the court had to draw a line.“It is because of our forgiving nature, that India is facing these problems. Forgive, forgive, forgive, you have to draw a line somewhere,” Justice Datta said, according to PTI.The judge then referred to a case in which the Supreme Court had commuted the death sentence of a man who had raped and murdered his elder daughter. Justice Datta said the man was sentenced to life imprisonment based on the testimony of the mother.After spending years in prison, the man was released on parole and allegedly murdered the mother in front of his younger daughter, Justice Datta said. The younger daughter's testimony subsequently led to the man being sentenced to death.Justice Datta noted that the Supreme Court later commuted that death sentence to life imprisonment on the ground that the man had not murdered the younger daughter.“That is why we say, our forgiving nature has to come to an end somewhere,” he said, as reported by Bar and Bench.

Article Title: CAPF law comes into force, mandates IPS quota in senior posts

NEW DELHI: The Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Act, 2026 — which stipulates that 50% of the posts in CAPFs at the level of Inspector General, a minimum 67% posts at the level of Additional Director General and 100% posts at level of Director General and Special Director General-level, be filled by IPS officers on deputation — came into force on Thursday.The home ministry, in a notification, specified October 8, 2026 as the “appointed day” on which the provisions of the Act shall come into force.The operationalisation of the IPS quota in senior CAPF posts comes days after Union home secretary Govind Mohan told the Supreme Court that deputation of 46 IPS officers across five paramilitary forces — CRPF, BSF, CISF, ITBP and SSB — since the court’s May 26, 2025 direction for a gradual reduction in the number of IPS officers on deputation within two years, was as per the law since the SC had not held that such deputation should be discontinued altogether.While CAPF cadre officers are opposed to senior posts in CAPFs being “cornered” by IPS officers, on the grounds that it blocks their career progression, the govt has backed deputation of IPS officers, describing them as crucial to coordination between the Centre and the states in view of national and inter-state roles of the CAPFs.

NEW DELHI: Votes cast in five assembly constituencies and one Lok Sabha seat will be counted on Friday, with the results of the bypoll elections likely to be closely watched for broader political signals.The elections were held on October 6 in five assembly seats — Nandigram and Rejinagar in West Bengal, Madurantakam and Dharapuram in Tamil Nadu and Thattanchavady in Puducherry. The Lok Sabha seat of Nagaon in Assam also went to polls. Counting of votes will begin at 8am.The contests are not necessarily referendums on the governments in power, but they have acquired significance because they come at different points in the political transitions taking place in these states, particulary Tamil Nadu and West Bengal.The spotlight will be firmly on West Bengal, where the BJP replaced the TMC after 15 years in power. The Nandigram and Rejinagar results would perhaps offer an early indication of how the BJP is performing after moving from the opposition to government.Turnout was high in both seats, with nearly 80 per cent of the 5.24 lakh electors voting. Nandigram recorded 80.89 per cent polling and Rejinagar 80.08 per cent.The polling, however, was not without controversy as there were allegations of voter intimidation, booth-level irregularities and sporadic clashes.The arrest of Aam Janata Unnayan Party chief Humayun Kabir after a confrontation with police in Rejinagar and Congress' demand for repolling in both seats added to the political tension.Nandigram carries particular weight because of its history as the constituency was central to the anti-land acquisition movement that helped bring the TMC to power in 2011. Suvendu Adhikari defeated Mamata Banerjee there in the 2021 Assembly election and won the seat again in 2026, while retaining Bhabanipur, leading to the bypoll.The BJP has fielded Hasirani Rath, whose son Chandranath Rath, a former aide of Adhikari, was shot dead two days after the BJP won the Assembly election. Her candidature therefore added an emotional element to the contest.The Opposition vote is also divided as the TMC faction led by Mamata Banerjee withdrew its candidate and backed Congress nominee Milan Pradhan. A rival TMC faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee is contesting separately. The result could therefore indicate whether opposition coordination can translate into votes or whether the division benefits the BJP.Rejinagar presents a different contest where Humayun Kabir, who had won both Rejinagar and Nowda in the Assembly election, retained Nowda, leaving Rejinagar vacant. His AJUP has fielded his son Golam Nabi Azad. The contest includes candidates from the BJP, Mamata-led TMC, rival TMC faction, Congress and CPI(M).With a sizeable minority electorate, Rejinagar is particularly important for parties trying to consolidate or expand their respective support bases. For the Mamata-led TMC faction, it is also a test of whether it can retain support without relying on the familiar party name and symbol.Tamil Nadu's Madurantakam and Dharapuram bypolls will also be closely watched, particularly because they are the first electoral test for the TVK government after it came to power in May.The AIADMK is seeking to win back the two seats it lost to the TVK in the April Assembly election, making the results an early measure of whether the new ruling party has retained its electoral momentum.Madurantakam recorded 86.26 per cent turnout, while Dharapuram saw 80.30 per cent polling. Both figures were lower than in the Assembly election five months ago. Turnout fell by nearly seven percentage points in Madurantakam and about 9.5 percentage points in Dharapuram.Counting centres in both constituencies have been placed under three-tier security. The EVMs and VVPAT units were moved to sealed strongrooms after polling, with round-the-clock surveillance and central and state security personnel deployed at the sites.In Assam, the Nagaon Lok Sabha bypoll is being seen as a three-way contest between BJP candidate and former bureaucrat Devasish Sharma, Congress nominee and former MLA Sibamoni Bora, and AIUDF chief Mohammed Badruddin Ajmal.The seat fell vacant after Congress MP Pradyut Bordoloi, who had won Nagaon for a second consecutive term in 2024, left the party, contested the Dispur Assembly seat on a BJP ticket and won it.Around 76 per cent of Nagaon's 19.05 lakh electors voted. Fifteen candidates are in the fray, although the contest is expected to be primarily between the BJP, Congress and AIUDF candidates.In Puducherry, the Thattanchavady Assembly bypoll recorded 80.8 per cent turnout. The seat fell vacant after AINRC chief and Chief Minister N Rangasamy resigned from it while retaining Mangalam.By the end of Friday, the results across these six contests would provide more than individual winners and losers. In West Bengal, they will offer an early look at the BJP's ability to consolidate power and at the opposition's ability to regroup. Tamil Nadu will provide an initial test of the TVK's popularity after its assembly victory, while Nagaon will show how the BJP, Congress and AIUDF fare in a three-way contest.
Article Summary: Votes cast in five assembly constituencies and one Lok Sabha seat will be counted on Friday. The elections were held on October 6 in West Bengal, Madurantakam and Dharapuram in Tamil Nadu and Thattanchavady in Puducherry. Counting of votes will begin at 8am.

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan
Article Text:
File photo: Supreme Court of India Judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan (PTI Photo)

Detaching right to vote from citizen is like taking soul out of body: Bhuyan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Launching a scathing attack on special intensive revision (SIR) that has resulted in large-scale deletion of names from voter lists across states, Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution.Discounting the reasons given by govt and EC to justify SIR, which was upheld in the case of the revision of rolls in West Bengal by SC with modifications, Justice Bhuyan said, "No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of Constitution. I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution."He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad.Nalsar students, who had opposed CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation ceremony recently, came in for praise from Justice Bhuyan.Also read| Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman "One last word about the brilliant students of Nalsar. You have shown to the country and to the world what a university student, that too a student of law, should be. You are brilliant, you are bold, and you are brave," he said.Justice Bhuyan said a citizen’s right to vote was central to the holding of free and fair elections.“Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing,” he added.The SC judge said the right to vote or be included in the voters’ list could not be detached from the persona of an Indian citizen.Also read: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added. Justice Bhuyan said the Indian Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens: citizens with voting rights and citizens without voting rights. “Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution of India,” he said.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary,” he added, his remarks coinciding with attacks on EC and govt over SIR by the opposition and others.Justice Bhuyan said the right to vote was intertwined with India’s years of struggle against foreign rule. “It is a manifestation of our freedom achieved after so much struggle and sacrifice. Article 326 (universal adult franchise) cannot be tinkered with at all. No authority can do it, no court can condone it. No one is above Constitution,” he said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution. He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad. “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added.

Article Title: "I know how hard she works”: How Connor McDavid’s wife Lauren Kyle turned a business struggle into a five-venture empire while building her own path beyond the NHL spotlight
Article Text:
Connor McDavid’s wife Lauren Kyle turned a business struggle into a five-venture empire(Image via X)

Connor McDavid saw how hard Lauren Kyle was working behind the scenes

Lauren Kyle used that lesson to expand far beyond interior design

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lauren Kyle McDavid had always known she wanted to build something of her own, but turning her creative ideas into successful businesses came with a learning curve. The wife of Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid started with interior design before expanding into fashion, furniture, food and publishing. Behind that growth was a challenge she had to face early in her career: learning the business side of her creative work.That part of Lauren’s journey became more important as she took on more projects. By June 2025, she had several ventures under her name, while Connor had watched closely as she learned to turn her ideas into businesses. His support also came at a time when Lauren needed help taking her first company to the next level.Lauren spoke about her entrepreneurial journey in a June 8, 2025 interview with theScore. She explained that she had always pictured herself working for herself and had grown up around people who ran their own businesses. Her first major venture was Kyle & Co., an interior design company that gave her a place to turn her ideas into a career.However, creativity alone could not handle every part of running a growing company.Connor explained during the same theScore interview that creative people can sometimes struggle with the business side of their ideas. He had seen Lauren put considerable time and energy into Kyle & Co. and wanted to help her move the company forward.“I know how hard she works, and I know the time and energy that she puts into it,” Connor said while discussing Lauren’s business journey with theScore in June 2025.Connor had also given Lauren sessions with a business coach as a birthday gift a few years earlier. The support proved useful because Lauren wanted to grow beyond her first company without losing the creative side that had driven her from the beginning.Lauren later explained just how valuable that experience became for her. “Without my business coach, I definitely wouldn't be able to have this many businesses at one time,” she told theScore in June 2025. She said the coaching helped change her mindset and gave her a better understanding of how to grow as an entrepreneur.The business coaching became part of a much bigger change in Lauren’s career. By June 2025, her portfolio included Kyle & Co., Sports Club Atelier, Trove Living and Bar Trove, while she was also preparing a cookbook.Sports Club Atelier grew from Lauren’s interest in creating better-looking sports apparel. Trove Living gave her interior design work a furniture and showroom component, while Bar Trove brought her creative approach into the restaurant space in downtown Edmonton. Her cookbook followed the same idea by focusing on experiences such as dinner parties and girls’ weekends instead of simply dividing recipes into traditional categories.Lauren’s approach has remained consistent across those projects. She wants people to feel something when they enter a space, wear something she designed or experience something she created. That idea also explains why Connor has remained impressed by the work happening behind the scenes.“I get a front row seat to everything she’s building,” Connor said in theScore’s June 2025 profile.Lauren’s story is therefore about more than being Connor McDavid’s wife. She had to learn a side of business that did not come naturally to her, accepted help when she needed it and used that experience to build a much larger portfolio of her own.
Article Summary: Connor McDavid’s wife Lauren Kyle turned a business struggle into a five-venture empire. The wife of Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid started with interior design before expanding into fashion, furniture, food and publishing. By June 2025, she had several ventures under her name, while Connor had watched closely.

Article Title: ‘He called every week’: Ex-Pakistan cricketer reveals how Nana Patekar stood by his mother during illness
Article Text:
Nana Patekar

A career spanning nearly five decades

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The death of veteran actor Nana Patekar has prompted an outpouring of grief beyond India, with members of the Pakistani cricket fraternity also paying tribute to the celebrated performer. Former Pakistan cricketer Basit Ali has shared an emotional account of his long-standing friendship with the actor, remembering how Patekar remained in touch with him and supported his family through difficult periods.Patekar died at the age of 75 on October 8 after suffering a severe cardiac arrest at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa. He was found unconscious and taken to Manipal Hospital, where doctors attempted to revive him with continuous CPR. However, their efforts were unsuccessful, and he was declared dead.As news of his passing spread, Pakistani cricketer Umar Akmal remembered the actor in a social media post, while Basit shared a video reflecting on a personal connection that began in 1994 and continued for decades.Recalling when he first heard about Patekar's death, Basit spoke about the affection he had for the actor and how their association had endured over the years.“Early in the morning I heard sad news. Our very dear brother, friend, and living legend is no longer in this world—Nana Patekar Sahab has passed away. What a person he was; he acted in movies exactly as he was in real life. We had nicknamed Latif as 'Nana'. Because of Nana Patekar, we first talked back in 1994, and it all started from there,” Basit said.The former cricketer then recalled how Patekar would regularly call to check on his family, particularly during the period when his mother was hospitalised. According to Basit, the actor continued to offer emotional support after her death and later enquired about his own health when he suffered a heart problem.“Now there are so many memories. Usually, we spoke once or twice every month. When my mother was alive and in the hospital, Nana Ji called every week. He offered many prayers, talked at length with my mother, and listened to old stories. When my mother passed away, he told me, ‘Hey Basit, take care of yourself now’. And when I had my heart issue and returned home, I received a message asking about my health and telling me to call when I felt better. When I called him back, he inquired about how everything went, including the stent placement,” he added.Basit also remembered the informal conversations they shared about Patekar's films, saying the actor's personality away from the camera was much like the one audiences saw on screen. Their exchanges, he said, were marked by familiarity, warmth and humour.“He was such a wonderful human being. For people who only knew him through movies, he was the exact same person in real life as well. People praised him, and we were fortunate to have many conversations. Sometimes we would ask him about a specific scene in a movie, and he would playfully say, ‘Shut up, what do you know?’. The love and affection he gave as an elder was truly incredible,” he said.The news of Patekar's death was particularly difficult for Basit to accept. He recalled often referring to the actor as a 'young man' because he did not appear to be 75, with Patekar responding jokingly that they were both getting old.“I still can't believe this news. The man did not look 75 years old. I used to always call him ‘young man,’ and he would reply, 'Forget it, both you and I are old now'. It is deeply painful. And I will say one thing here: Nana Ji had as many admirers in Pakistan as he had in India and across the world. People loved him very much," he concluded his video.Patekar was one of the most recognisable names in Hindi and Marathi cinema, building a career that stretched across nearly five decades. He made his Hindi film debut with the 1978 film 'Gaman' before earning widespread recognition for his performances in a range of critically acclaimed and popular films.A defining moment came with Vidhu Vinod Chopra's 'Parinda' in 1989, in which his portrayal of the ruthless crime boss Anna won him the National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor. His filmography also included 'Prahar', 'Angaar', 'Krantiveer', 'Tiranga', 'Khamoshi' and 'Ab Tak Chhappan', among others.His contribution to cinema was recognised with the Padma Shri in 2013, India's fourth-highest civilian award. Away from films, Patekar was also associated with social initiatives, particularly efforts to support farmers and families affected by drought in Maharashtra.The veteran actor remained involved in films in recent years. He was part of 'Housefull 5', which featured Akshay Kumar, Abhishek Bachchan and Riteish Deshmukh, among others. He also played a police officer in Vishal Bhardwaj's 'O'Romeo', starring Shahid Kapoor and Tripti Dimri, and had a cameo in 'Subedar', featuring Anil Kapoor and Radhika Madan.
Article Summary: Patekar died at the age of 75 on October 8 after suffering a severe cardiac arrest at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa. Pakistani cricketer Umar Akmal remembered the actor in a social media post, while Basit Ali shared a video reflecting on a personal connection that began in 1994.

Article Title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ $325 million KC Current stadium expansion gets green light with $185 million funding
Article Text:
Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes (Instagram)

Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ KC Current investment grows

CPKC Stadium expansion could transform Kansas City’s Riverfront

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Kansas City Current are preparing for a much bigger future at CPKC Stadium, and the latest move could reshape the club’s place in women’s soccer. Kansas City has approved $185 million in public funding for the stadium expansion, paving the way for thousands of new seats and major improvements around the Riverfront. For co-owners Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes , the project adds another major chapter to a club they have helped build from the ground up. The expansion also strengthens Kansas City’s bid to attract major international sporting events and turn the Riverfront into an even bigger destination for fans.The Mahomes connection to the Kansas City Current goes beyond Patrick’s profile as the Chiefs’ star quarterback. Brittany Mahomes was part of the original ownership group that brought the NWSL franchise to Kansas City, while Patrick joined the ownership team in 2023. The Current officially lists both as co-owners, alongside Angie Long and Chris Long.That gives the stadium expansion added significance for the Mahomes family. CPKC Stadium opened in 2024 with 11,500 seats and quickly became a major symbol of the growth of women’s professional sports. Now, the proposed work would increase capacity to 18,000.The plan calls for about 6,500 additional seats, mainly in the corners between the existing grandstands.The club also intends to raise the roofline, add more premium boxes and double its suite capacity.For a team that has already attracted strong crowds, the larger venue could give the Current more room to build its audience while creating additional opportunities for premium hospitality and major events.The stadium project is part of a much larger transformation of the Berkley Riverfront area. The broader $1.4 billion development is expected to bring new housing, retail, parking and infrastructure improvements, creating a district designed to remain active beyond match days.The Current also sees the expanded stadium as a potential gateway to major international events. Kansas City is looking ahead to opportunities such as the 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup and the Men’s Rugby World Cup, making venue capacity and facilities increasingly important.There is also a financial safeguard attached to the public funding. The team and its development partners have committed to covering the city’s bond debt if tax revenue does not generate enough money to meet those payments.Construction on the stadium expansion is expected to begin after next season. If completed as planned, CPKC Stadium will offer the Current a significantly larger stage while helping reshape Kansas City’s Riverfront into a year-round sports and entertainment destination.
Article Summary: The Kansas City Current are preparing for a much bigger future at CPKC Stadium. Kansas City has approved $185 million in public funding for the stadium expansion, paving the way for thousands of new seats. The expansion also strengthens Kansas City’s bid to attract major international sporting events.

Article Title: “We’re thrilled to partner”: How Patrick Mahomes’ mom Randi Mahomes helped raise more than $150,000 for children with disabilities through charity event
Article Text:
Patrick Mahomes’ mom Randi Mahomes helped raise more than $150,000 for children with disabilities (Getty Images)

Randi Mahomes ’ Heart & Serve event raised more than $150,000

Randi Mahomes had a personal connection to the cause

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Randi Mahomes found another way to use her connection with Kansas City sports to help children. Patrick Mahomes ’ mom teamed up with Variety KC for the first Heart & Serve pickleball tournament on Sept. 14, 2024. The event brought sports families and local supporters together while raising more than $150,000 for children with disabilities. Randi also took part in the tournament and helped bring attention to a cause she has supported for years.Variety KC announced its partnership with Patrick Mahomes mom, Randi Mahomes on Aug. 12, 2024. The organisation planned the inaugural Heart & Serve tournament for Sept. 14 at the Kansas City Convention Center. Randi served as the event's emcee and joined other professional sports moms and wives at the charity event.The fundraiser had a clear goal. Proceeds would support Variety KC and its work with children who have special needs and disabilities. The organisation helps families get medical equipment and services for mobility, sensory needs, communication, safety and therapy.The event also had a strong local sports connection. Randi was joined by 18 other professional sports moms and wives.The day included pickleball matches and family activities. The organisers also planned the event as an accessible and family-friendly gathering.Then came the number that showed the reach of the fundraiser. According to a Variety KC and SERVfun update the Kansas City community raised more than $150,000 to support children with disabilities through the event.That figure is important because Randi did not simply attach her name to a charity event. She helped bring together people from the local sports community for a fundraiser with a direct focus on children.Randi's involvement with Variety KC did not start with Heart & Serve. She had supported the organisation through birthday fundraising campaigns and other charity efforts before the pickleball tournament.Variety KC also had a strong connection with the Mahomes family. In an August 9, 2024 report about Heart & Serve, Variety KC said it was excited about the Mahomes family's support and the chance to introduce its work to a larger Kansas City audience.Marc Harrell, Variety KC's chief inclusion officer and executive director, also spoke about the partnership before the tournament. In the August 2024 announcement, he said, “We are thrilled to partner with Randi Mahomes and other incredible athletes’ families for this unique event.” He added that the event gave the community a chance to come together through sports and philanthropy.The tournament then gave Randi a chance to get involved on the court as well.After Heart & Serve on September 14, 2024, Randi shared her reaction to the event and said, “This was so much fun.” She made the comment after taking part in the Variety KC charity pickleball tournament.Variety KC also thanked the people who supported the event. In its post about the fundraiser, the charity called it “an amazing day” and thanked everyone who helped make Heart & Serve a success.For Randi, the event added another chapter to her long-running connection with Variety KC. Her charity work has included fundraising for adaptive equipment and other resources for children with disabilities.Heart & Serve simply gave that work a new setting. Instead of a football field, Randi brought people together around pickleball. The result was more than a day of sport. It helped the Kansas City community raise more than $150,000 for children who needed greater access to equipment, activities and support.
Article Summary: Patrick Mahomes’ mom Randi Mahomes teamed up with Variety KC for the first Heart & Serve pickleball tournament on Sept. 14, 2024. The event brought sports families and local supporters together while raising more than $150,000 for children with disabilities. Randi also took part in the tournament and helped bring attention to a cause she has supported for years.

Article Title: Caitlin Clark donated $2,000 to honor late Indiana Fever supporter through community fundraiser

Caitlin Clark (Image via Getty)

Caitlin Clark continues connection with Fever fans

In August, Caitlin Clark made a quiet gesture that carried special meaning for an Indiana Fever supporter’s family. The fundraiser is focused on turning Jess’ love for her community into something lasting, with donations helping place Buddy Benches and books in local classrooms.Clark’s contribution came after Jess died, leaving behind a community of supporters who had followed her enthusiasm for the Fever and the team’s star guard. Its goal is to create useful resources for children in local classrooms. Funds will support Buddy Benches and provide books, giving Jess’ memory a place within the community she cared about.A supporter account, Caitlin Clark Style, shared the news on X:“Caitlin donated to Jess’s @FeverBandwagon GoFundMe 🥺✨The fundraiser will provide Buddy Benches and books for local classrooms in Jess’s memory.”The gesture also reflects the relationship Clark has built with Fever fans since entering the WNBA.
