Article Title: America has enjoyed the greatest free lunch in history: Vivek Wadhwa reacts to Green Card crackdown on 8 IT companies, says they aren't the visa abusers
Article Text:
Green Card crackdown on major IT giants including Microsoft shakes Silicon Valley.

Microsoft only files H-1B petitions for those...

JD Vance on IT bodyshops

Indian-American entrepreneur Vivek Wadhwa strongly reacted to the Donald Trump administration's suspension PERM program for eight IT giants, including Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL Technologies, and Capegemini and said that these companies are not the visa abusers. The visa abusers are those who recruit for these companies or the IT bodyshops and they need to be shut down, Wadhwa said."America has enjoyed the greatest free lunch in history: highly educated, highly skilled immigrants bringing their talent to its shores. Now it’s snatching defeat from the jaws of victory by turning away the truly best and brightest. These companies aren’t the visa abusers. The body shops exploiting the system are the ones that need to be shut down," Wadhwa said, defending Silicon Valley.Suspending PERM process means the H-1B visa holders working in these companies can't take the Green Card route. However, it is not known whether the suspension will eventually be lifted.Nasscom, the apex body of Indian IT companies, called it a temporary suspension and said that it believes that immigration and skilled talent mobility are two separate issues and should not be viewed through the same lens."The H-1B visa program has historically played an important role in addressing short-term skill gaps in the US, and it will continue to be used to address short-term talent gap.However, over a number of years, Indian technology companies have significantly reduced their dependence on H-1B visas, while steadily expanding local hiring and building a strong domestic workforce in the US. They work with majority of the US Fortune 500 companies. .."Microsoft also issued a statement against the damaging allegation of visa fraud and said Microsoft only files H-1B petitions for those who meet the rigorous standards of this visa category. "We pay our employees some of the highest compensation in the tech sector, and our wages are among the highest of all H-1B filings. We pay our H-1B employees the same as any other employees doing comparable work," it said.Microsoft said it is ready to provide additional information to the administration. "For example, of the approximately 6,000 H-1B visa applications we submitted in the last fiscal year, 80% percent were to extend or change the status of existing Microsoft employees. These were not to hire new people. The remaining filings for new employees were for individuals already legally in the United States who decided to come work for us, and they equal only 1% of our U.S. workforce. They are not new arrivals to our country," it said.JD Vance, in his statement, mentioned the IT bodyshops that recruit the H-1Bs on behalf of these IT giants but the administration decided to shake the big players to make an impact, instead of chasing the thousands of small staffing companies."If you are working as an H-1B visa in the United States of America, you’re earning $20,000 less than an American citizen hired in the same position. If you were brought in by one of these foreign outsourcing firms, you’re making $48,000 less than an American citizen in a similar position. So I’m sure that everybody here understands the game that is being played. You bring in indentured servants from outside the country, you lay off American workers and, if you’re a corporation, you make a ton of money by undercutting the wages of American workers, replacing them with people who frankly shouldn’t be in the United States of America to begin with," Vance said.
Article Summary: Suspending PERM process means the H-1B visa holders working in these companies can't take the Green Card route. It is not known whether the suspension will eventually be lifted. Indian-American entrepreneur Vivek Wadhwa strongly reacted to the Donald Trump administration's suspension PERM program.

Article Title: Jon Jones finally remembers longtime “frenemy” Daniel Cormier after struggling through hilarious pizza challenge
Article Text:
“Your logic doesn’t make any sense”: Jon Jones challenges Colby Covington after Gable Steveson loss as former college roommates reignite their bitter rivalry

Jon Jones calls on Daniel Cormier for help during pizza challenge

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jon Jones has once again brought Daniel Cormier into the spotlight, but this time in a much lighter way. The former UFC champion appeared to remember his longtime rival while taking part in a pizza challenge. After only a few bites, Jones joked that he needed help from Cormier to get through the challenge.Jones and Cormier shared one of the fiercest rivalries in UFC history. Their rivalry featured heated exchanges, a famous media-day brawl and two championship fights. While their relationship has become more cordial over the years, Cormier has made it clear that the two are not friends. Jones’ latest comment, however, showed that their rivalry can still produce plenty of laughs.During a recent pizza challenge, Jon Jones appeared to struggle after eating only a few bites. The moment prompted him to jokingly call on the man who was once his biggest rival inside the UFC.“I have never wanted to see Daniel Cormier more than I want to see him right now. Tag in brother”, he said.The comment became a funny reminder of one of the most famous rivalries in MMA history. Jones and Cormier spent years trading verbal shots and building intense animosity before finally settling their differences inside the Octagon.Their first fight took place at UFC 182 in January 2015. Jones entered the bout as the UFC light heavyweight champion and defeated Cormier by unanimous decision. The fight was the culmination of years of tension between the two fighters.The rivalry became even more heated before their first meeting. In 2014, Jones and Cormier were involved in a wild confrontation during a UFC 178 media event. The two fighters got into a physical altercation during their face-off, with the incident spilling from the stage into the lobby.They eventually met again at UFC 214 in July 2017. Jones stopped Cormier with a third-round head kick and punches. However, the result was later overturned to a No Contest after Jones tested positive for turinabol. Jones was stripped of the title, while Cormier was reinstated as champion.Despite the bitter history, their relationship has changed over time. The two have been able to appear together professionally and interact without the same level of hostility that defined their rivalry during their fighting careers.However, Cormier has previously explained that he does not consider Jones a friend. Their history remains too complicated, particularly because of the controversies surrounding Jones’ drug-testing history.Cormier retired from MMA in 2020 after completing his trilogy with Stipe Miocic. Jones later moved to heavyweight and became the UFC heavyweight champion.Their competitive careers have taken them in different directions. Yet moments like Jones’ pizza challenge comment show that Cormier remains a familiar name in his mind. This time, there was no Octagon, championship belt or heated face-off involved.
Article Summary: Jon Jones and Daniel Cormier shared one of the fiercest rivalries in UFC history. Their rivalry featured heated exchanges, a famous media-day brawl and two championship fights. While their relationship has become more cordial over the years, Cormier has made it clear that they are not friends.

Article Title: How did Jason Kelce go from criticising NFL referees to defending them? His stance shifted after two controversial incidents
Article Text:
Jason Kelce go from criticising NFL referees to defending them(Getty)

Jason Kelce initially backed Eric Wilson after his clash with Adrian Hill

Trey McBride incident and NFL referee suspensions spark a wider debate

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jason Kelce had plenty to say about the NFL ’s decision to suspend two officials after separate on-field incidents involving Trey McBride and Eric Wilson. The retired Philadelphia Eagles center initially criticised referee Adrian Hill for his treatment of Wilson during the Minnesota Vikings’ game against the Miami Dolphins. However, Kelce later changed his position during an episode of New Heights, the podcast he hosts with his brother, Travis Kelce The debate grew after the NFL suspended Hill for one game and line judge Jeff Seeman for two games on Oct. 5, 2026. Both officials faced discipline for what the league described as unprofessional conduct toward a player. Kelce’s change of stance added another twist to a controversy that has raised questions about how the NFL should hold officials accountable when tempers flare during games.During the Vikings-Dolphins game in Week 4, Miami running back Ollie Gordon II knocked Minnesota linebacker Eric Wilson into Hill, sending the referee to the ground. Hill got back up and shouted at Wilson, who appeared to be trying to help him stand.Kelce criticised the official’s response during New Heights, arguing that Wilson had not deliberately knocked Hill down. He said, “I have a bigger problem with this one.'Cause clearly Eric Wilson did not try to do this. And then he’s trying to help him up, and then he gets mad at him. I think this is bogus.”His initial reaction focused on the circumstances behind the collision. Wilson had not appeared to intentionally bring Hill down, yet the exchange escalated after the official got back to his feet. The incident became one of two high-profile officiating controversies that prompted the NFL to review its officials’ conduct.However, Kelce did not stick with that position for long. Later in the same podcast discussion, he reconsidered his response and announced that he was retracting his criticism.“You know what? I’m retracting all this! I’m on the sides of both of these officials! I take the officials’ side!” Kelce said on New Heights””.His reversal gave the discussion a new direction, especially as the NFL faced criticism over the punishments handed to Hill and Seeman.The other controversy involved Seeman and Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride. During Arizona’s 36-24 loss to the New York Giants, Seeman appeared to direct profanity at McBride after a third-down incompletion. McBride had disputed the lack of a pass-interference penalty against Giants cornerback Dru Phillips.Video of the exchange circulated online before the NFL announced Seeman’s two-game suspension on October 5. Hill received a one-game suspension for his interaction with Wilson.The NFL Referees Association challenged the severity of the penalties. On Tuesday, October 6, executive director Scott Green acknowledged that the officials’ conduct fell short of professional standards but argued that referees regularly face heated exchanges and verbal abuse from players and coaches.The NFL Players Association took a firmer stance on Seeman’s conduct. Executive director JC Tretter said officials should face the same standards as players when they cross the line.The league has disciplined players for their treatment of officials, too. In October 2025, Denver Broncos linebacker Dre Greenlaw received a one-game suspension without pay after chasing referee Brad Allen and verbally threatening him following Denver’s 33-32 win over the New York Giants. His appeal failed.Kelce’s change of heart did not settle the argument. Instead, it highlighted the difficult balance between protecting officials and holding them accountable. With the referees’ union challenging the suspensions, the NFL now faces further scrutiny over how it handles misconduct on both sides of the whistle.
Article Summary: Jason Kelce initially criticised referee Adrian Hill for his treatment of Eric Wilson during the Minnesota Vikings’ game against the Miami Dolphins. However, Kelce later changed his position during an episode of New Heights, the podcast he hosts with his brother, Travis Kelce. The debate grew after the NFL suspended Hill for one game and line judge Jeff Seeman for two games on October 5, 2026.

Article Title: Never give up! Nic Maddinson’s remarkable journey from testicular cancer and chemotherapy to an unexpected Australia Test comeback
Article Text:
Nic Maddinson (X)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

When Nic Maddinson told his four-year-old son August that he was heading to South Africa, the youngster began listing the animals he knew lived there. The family even squeezed in some cricket in the hallway of their Byron Bay home before Maddinson left for what could become one of the most significant chapters of his career.For the left-handed batter, however, the journey back to Australia’s Test team has been about far more than cricket. It has been a story of battling testicular cancer, enduring chemotherapy and finding a new perspective on life before earning an unexpected return to the national set-up.Maddinson discovered a lump last year, and scans revealed testicular cancer. He underwent surgery to remove it, but further tests seven weeks later showed the cancer had spread to parts of his abdominal lymph nodes and lung.At the time, his wife Bianca was pregnant with their second child. She gave up her job as a dentist to care for their toddler, August, while Maddinson underwent treatment.His days became a difficult routine of hospital visits, rest and trying to eat before attempting to sleep again. He completed chemotherapy on July 14, but had to wait another two months before receiving clearance to resume full training.The birth of his second son, Wilder, brought another source of joy as Maddinson began rebuilding his life and cricket career.Having come through the ordeal, he has also urged others to seek medical attention if they notice anything unusual.His return to competitive cricket has been remarkable. Maddinson last played first-class cricket in March 2025, meaning he went 579 days without a match in the format before returning to Australia's Test set-up. It is the longest such gap for an Australian before a men's Test match.The call-up itself came as a surprise. When George Bailey , the chair of selectors, rang him, Maddinson initially wondered whether the conversation might concern an Australia A tour of India or another young player.“I thought maybe he was calling me to go to India for the A tour or ask about another young player around because I was a little bit unsure what was going on,” Maddinson said.He admitted he had not believed himself to be close to a Test recall, although the hope of returning had never disappeared.“Obviously didn't feel like I was that close but still had hopes of maybe one day getting back into a Test squad. So, in terms of motivation, it's still always been there but yeah definitely a bit of a surprise.”The 34-year-old spent much of the long flight to South Africa processing the news, trying to relax with sleep and films while reflecting on what he described as one of the “craziest” weekends of his life.Despite the lengthy break from first-class cricket, Maddinson said he was confident about his physical conditioning. He had been playing matches and multi-day red-ball games with New South Wales as he worked towards regaining his fitness.His outlook on cricket has also changed since his previous Test appearance against Pakistan at the MCG in 2016. A decade of first-class experience, combined with his health battle, has helped him find greater balance and confidence in his game.“I always felt like I understood the game pretty well but when you look back I feel like you probably don't know that much,” he said.He believes he has learnt not to force himself into a particular style simply to satisfy selectors or secure his place in the side, instead developing the ability to adapt to different conditions.Now back in the Test environment, Maddinson has been welcomed by teammates who know him from years of playing alongside or against him. His return also reunites him with coach Andrew McDonald, under whom he honed his skills during his time in Victoria.The comeback is already a powerful story of resilience. After cancer treatment, a lengthy absence from first-class cricket and the uncertainty of whether another Test opportunity would come, Maddinson has earned his way back.For August, the trip may be about South Africa’s animals and geography. For his father, it represents something far bigger: a return to the game after overcoming a battle that put life itself into perspective.
Article Summary: Nic Maddinson has returned to Australia's Test set-up. The 34-year-old last played first-class cricket in March 2025. It is the longest such gap for an Australian before a men's Test match. Maddinson discovered a lump last year, and scans revealed testicular cancer.

Article Title: OpenAI tells the world why it fired three of its top researchers; writes open letter saying, ‘Our internal investigation uncovered…’
Article Text:
What note from OpenAI research leaders said

A note from our research leaders:

Last week we parted ways with Jasmine, Mikita, and Tomek after a thorough investigation found they violated clear policies on handling sensitive information.

Our internal investigation uncovered a significant breach of trust beyond what’s outlined in the letter they published and we stand by the decision to not continue their employment. We generally keep individual employment matters private and don't believe a back and forth would be productive or lead to a resolution, but we want to address the points they raised in their letter directly.

- We want to be very clear that these decisions were not about raising safety concerns or speaking out.

Safety and research debates happen every day at OpenAI, often spirited and highly critical. We actively encourage these discussions and consider them essential to making the right decisions. We cannot do the work in front of us without a high degree of trust. We will continue to be extremely forgiving of our team making good-faith mistakes.

We have not and do not terminate any of our employees for raising concerns.

- We are actively finalizing contracts with third-party safety assessors and will announce details in the coming weeks.

People across the company have been working really hard on getting these partnerships up and running. We are committed to embedding external assessors and continue to make close collaboration with independent safety organizations a core part of our safety work. Many of our researchers already work with 3p safety organizations productively.

- We agree with the letter that preserving the monitorability of frontier models requires an industry-wide commitment, including from OpenAI.

Monitorability has long been a core piece of our research program, and something we continue to invest significant resources in (see our publications on Monitoring Monitorability and the subsequent open sourcing of monitorability evals, our system card for GPT-6 Astra, Jakub’s blog and post on X, and the numerous blog posts on our Alignment blog on the topic).

We are deeply sad about this outcome. We appreciated Jasmine, Mikita, and Tomek’s contributions to AI safety at OpenAI and their willingness to speak up and challenge ideas.

We championed their voices, supported their work, and placed enormous trust in them. These decisions were not about them raising safety concerns. We have always encouraged that and always will.

Fired engineers publish letter to OpenAI board
Article Summary: A note from OpenAI's research leaders addresses the firing of three engineers. The engineers violated policies on handling sensitive information, the note says. The company says it is committed to embedding external safety assessors in its research program. The team will continue to be extremely forgiving of our team making good-faith mistakes, it says.

Article Title: Zak Bagans paid $4.55 million for a 16,936-sq-ft Las Vegas home hidden 26 feet underground; once listed at $18 million, the Cold War-era bunker near the Strip will now become a public museum
Article Text:
For Bagans, whose career revolves around exploring the paranormal and preserving objects associated with unexplained phenomena, the property offers an opportunity to create another distinctive museum experience.

A hidden world beneath the city

Built for a Cold War world

From an $18 million listing to a $4.55 million sale

A new attraction for curious visitors

Beneath the neon-lit spectacle of the Las Vegas Strip lies a world that seems to belong to another era, where painted skies replace the real thing and landscaped interiors create the illusion of life above ground. Built to offer refuge from the anxieties of the Cold War, an extraordinary subterranean residence is now preparing for a new chapter, this time as a museum dedicated to its unusual history. Paranormal investigator and Ghost Adventures host Zak Bagans has purchased the sprawling property for $4.55 million, with plans to eventually open its doors to the public, states an online report by Realtor.According to Realtor, known as the Underground House, the 16,936-square-foot property sits 26 feet below ground and features five bedrooms, an indoor swimming pool, a putting green, a theatre, a dance floor and a bar. A programmable artificial sky completes the setting, recreating the atmosphere of an outdoor landscape without exposing residents to the world above.Located just minutes from the Las Vegas Strip, the home is difficult to identify from street level. Its subterranean design, complete with landscape murals, painted clouds and stars, sculpted trees concealing structural columns, a water fountain and green carpeting resembling grass, was conceived to make underground living feel surprisingly ordinary, adds the online report.For Bagans, whose career revolves around exploring the paranormal and preserving objects associated with unexplained phenomena, the property offers an opportunity to create another distinctive museum experience, explains the report.According to Realtor, the residence was constructed in 1978 by businessman Jerry Henderson and architect Jay Swayze. Conceived as an Atomitat, or atomic habitat, it reflected an era when fears of nuclear conflict encouraged people to imagine alternative ways of living and surviving. Henderson lived there with his wife, Mary, until his death in 1983. She later built a smaller, conventional house above the underground structure, choosing to live there until her death in 1989.Over the decades, the unusual property evolved beyond its original purpose. Its subterranean rooms were eventually used for special events, while a house manager occupied the home above ground.The property's real estate journey has been almost as remarkable as its design. The Stasis Foundation & Charitable Trust purchased it in March 2014 for $1.15 million. Five years later, it entered the market with an ambitious asking price of $18 million. After failing to attract a buyer, the asking price was subsequently reduced to $5.9 million.Bagans ultimately secured the property for $4.55 million, marking a significant drop from its original multimillion-dollar listing. Its unusual architecture and elaborate history also made viewings an undertaking in themselves. Prospective buyers were carefully screened, with tours lasting several hours to accommodate explanations of the home's origins and features, claims the online report.Bagans already operates Zak Bagans' The Haunted Museum in downtown Las Vegas, where visitors explore rooms filled with reportedly haunted objects and items associated with paranormal stories. The Underground House could offer a different experience, blending architectural curiosity, Cold War history and the intrigue surrounding a home concealed beneath an otherwise ordinary neighbourhood. Its planned transformation into a public museum will also help preserve a rare example of experimental underground living. In a city renowned for spectacle, the next attraction may be one that visitors have to descend below ground to discover, concludes the report.Images Courtesy: Wikipedia and Realtor
Article Summary: The 16,936-square-foot property sits 26 feet below ground and features five bedrooms, an indoor swimming pool, a theatre, a dance floor and a bar. Paranormal investigator and Ghost Adventures host Zak Bagans has purchased the sprawling property for $4.55 million, with plans to eventually open its doors to the public.

Article Title: Kovai Heroes: When an accident survivor turned a guardian angel on Coimbatore city roads
Article Text:
V S Suresh Kumar

Kovai Heroes is a city-wide recognition initiative by The Times of India, presented by Infinium Developers to identify, celebrate, and honour individuals making a positive impact in Coimbatore through service, innovation, and leadership. Education Partner: SSVM Institutions. Associate Partner: Lakshmi Ceramics.





COIMBATORE: He wears no khaki uniform and carries no challan books, yet motorists in Coimbatore often mistake 55-year-old V S Suresh Kumar for a vigilant traffic officer. Armed with high-visibility reflective tape, a microphone and an uncompromising stance on road discipline, Suresh roams at city junctions and on arterial bypasses, coaxing drivers to choose life over haste. When he spots a freight auto or a minitruck without rear markings, he flags it down -- not to penalize the driver, but to paste reflective strips on the tailgate himself."Driving responsibly is a collective duty," says Suresh, a resident of Saibaba Colony. "Every commuter has someone waiting for them back home. Our ultimate goal must be zero road fatalities."Suresh became a road safety crusader after he met with an accident on a city road in 2008. He was riding on a motorcycle through Avarampalayam without a helmet. Three college students on a speeding bike rode in from the wrong direction, colliding head-on with his motorcycle. The impact was unforgiving. For seven harrowing days, Suresh lay motionless on a hospital bed.He survived the ordeal without an invasive brain surgery, but the man who woke up had changed forever. A native of Virudhunagar who moved to Coimbatore in 1989 as a corporate vehicle supervisor, Suresh realized that the margin between survival and death was very thin."When I regained consciousness after a week in the dark, the very first thought that gripped me was that no one should ever suffer what I went through," he recalls.That vow transformed into Vizhi - Awake, a dedicated road-safety mission launched in 2011. Suresh started out in a beat-up minivan. Later, he received support from the Rotary Club, which provided a multi-utility vehicle fitted with loudspeakers.Standing at dangerous intersections, Suresh directly halts errant riders. He does not scold; he reasons, explaining the blunt realities of a crash. He is equally intentional in his praise: motorists faithfully wearing helmets are stopped, lauded and presented with small gifts like lunch boxes.The impact of his intervention hit home recently when a motorcyclist called him in tears. Weeks after Suresh had stopped him for riding without a helmet and persuaded him to wear headgear, the man was thrown off his two-wheeler in a brutal crash. His limbs were badly fractured, but his head remained intact. "I am alive today only because you stopped me that day," the rider told him.Today, videos on Suresh’s YouTube channel have found widespread resonance, prompting invitations from across Tamil Nadu. Every day, he takes to Coimbatore's streets and ensures that a stranger reaches home safely.
Article Summary: V S Suresh Kumar, 55, is a road safety crusader in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu. Armed with high-visibility reflective tape, a microphone and an uncompromising stance on road discipline, he roams at city junctions and on arterial bypasses. Every day, he ensures that a stranger reaches home safely.

Article Title: Five decades and an evolving artist: Looking at Kanchan Chander's 50-year-journey
Article Text:
A visitor at the exhibition admires Kanchan Chander artwork titled Khajuraho II. The artist’s journey has been shaped by her travels, which led to thematic series such as Punks, Noses and Bhuta Aradhana

Kanchan Chander paints on curator Kishore Singh’s shirt

When I started as an artist life 50 years ago, I was very docile, quiet and a very conscious person. Over the years, I have become a strong, opinionated woman. That’s how my art and I evolved Kanchan Chander, artist and printmaker

'The body of work shows that Kanchan has understood that there are infinite possibilities'

Constant evolution of an artist is very important: Kanchan

Kishore Singh, Kanchan Chander and Roobina Karode

Amitava Das, Maite Delteil and Mona Rai

Vipul Kumar and Rahul Kumar

Biman Das and Jayasri Burman

Pallav Chander; Chilean Ambassador Juan Angulo with wife Patricia Vrij





Kanchan Chander didn’t need a canvas to demonstrate her artistry. At the opening of her retrospective earlier this week, The Grammar of the Self, at Bikaner House, curator Kishore Singh, in a playful moment, asked her to show the audience that she could paint. She picked up a brush, dipped it in black paint and with characteristic flair, painted a face – complete with the distinctive nose that has appeared in her work – on the front of his shirt. She then painted a female torso on the back. The impromptu artwork was an apt introduction to an exhibition that brings together five decades of Kanchan’s practice – from early self-portraits and figurative drawings to etchings, prints, mixed-media works and her recent geometric drawings.Presented by Gallery Ragini, the exhibition unfolds almost like a visual autobiography. It begins with self-portraits that the curator described as “guarded, cautious, reflective, internalised”, then moves through works shaped by personal experiences, travels, and her enduring engagement with the female form.For Kanchan, the retrospective is about evolution – of both the artist and the woman."The roller-coaster life I've had has been reflected here. It is interpreted through the grammar. These are the phases of my life. Right in the beginning, when I was in college, when my brother passed away in 1980. my marriage, which was not a happy one, the birth of my child – all this has been reflected in phases of four or five years in the works, in different forms," she shared, adding, "I feel the constant evolution of an artist is very important. "For Kishore, this ability to transform personal experience without remaining confined to it is central to understanding an artist’s practice. “Kanchan’s visual language is deeply autobiographical without ever becoming self-absorbed,” he observed.Art curator Roobina Karode pointed to the breadth of Kanchan's practice and said, "She used to make elongated or crouching (female) torsos. Then she started making incomplete torsos, and you see how that idea of the incomplete figure keeps translating through her practice. The body of work shows that Kanchan has understood that there are infinite possibilities. And that is perhaps the most important lesson she has learned — that she could be honest to herself, and not jump on any bandwagon. She could shift and move from one mode of drawing to another, and then another."
Article Summary: The Grammar of the Self, at Bikaner House, is a retrospective of Kanchan Chander's work. It brings together five decades of her practice – from self- portraits and figurative drawings to etchings, prints, mixed-media works and recent geometric drawings.

One outfit. Multiple festivals. Zero guilt. The old festive dressing rule — new event, new outfit — is getting a Gen Z rewrite. Why buy another lehenga when the one sitting in your cupboard can have a completely different personality with a new pair of shoes, a different drape or a borrowed jacket?For a generation that likes its fashion personal, practical and a little experimental, repeating an outfit isn't exactly repeating the look. It’s about reimagining what you already own or what is accessible to you. This festive season, Mumbai Gen Zs show us how.Richa Jain, a third-year BBA student from Lalbaug, isn't interested in collecting outfits for one-time appearances. She’s taking one look from a wedding straight into Navratri — with a footwear switch. “I am a budget paglu! So, I bargained a lot for this outfit. Buying a new outfit for each event and party can become expensive and wasteful, and I believe in repeat dressing. I wore this for my brother's wedding and now I’m going to repeat it during Navratri, and pair it with sneakers. This is very comfortable so I can play garba very well in it.” Same outfit. Different vibe. That’s the point.Why shop when there’s an entire archive sitting at home? Hiya K Mehta, a mass-media student who loves putting together festive looks, went straight to her mother’s wardrobe and turned a sari into something completely different.“I really loved my mom’s ombre bandhni sari in pink-orange and so I made this Indo-western outfit with it. I created this long shrug and wore it with a pair of blue jeans and a white tank top and accessorized it with oxidized jewellery. I believe that your mom’s closet can be a treasure trove!” And suddenly, an old sari becomes a new fit.For Ronak Thakkar, a third-year Mass Media student from Kandivali, festive dressing comes with a little thrift-store hunting. “I’ve thrifted this garba-ready denim jacket. Preloved thrifted fashion is a good route to choose during the festive season. I feel the bonus is that with this you are far less likely to turn up at a festive event wearing the exact same outfit as someone else.” Because honestly, the best festive outfit might be the one nobody else has.Not everything in your festive wardrobe has to belong to you. Sometimes, it just needs to look good on you. Vrinda Talati, a first-year BBA student, borrowed her festive outfit from a friend rather than buying one for herself. “I think borrowing clothes is actually a practical way to dress for festivals. We often buy festive outfits and wear them only once or twice, so instead of buying something new, I borrowed this one from a friend and styled it in my own way. Borrowing saves money, gives me more options, and is a more sustainable approach to fashion. I think what matters is how confidently and creatively you wear an outfit, not whether you own it.” The flex isn't owning the outfit. It's what you do with it.You don't need a new garment. You need a new combination.

Why buy another lehenga when the one sitting in your cupboard can have a completely different personality with a new pair of shoes, a different drape or a borrowed jacket? Mumbai Gen Zs show us how.

Article Title: Garba the traditional way: 500 college students revive the spirit of the festival
Article Text:
Singer Bhoomi Trivedi's presence was one of the highlights of the event

DID YOU KNOW?





Earlier this week, over 500 college students in traditional garba finery gathered for what was, remarkably, an exam. For 90 minutes they danced in age-old concentric circles, with the Mataji sthapana at the centre, as the singer Bhoomi Trivedi lifted the evening with her presence.Bhoomi said she felt a touch of Vadodara in the formation, one of the few places where Navratri is still danced this way. For Jigar Soni, the senior garba instructor that was the whole point. "The young generation has to learn to celebrate garba as a festival, not an event," he says.For the students, the experience was a lesson in culture, devotion and community. Anahita Thageshwar, one of the participants, says, “Dancing with more than 500 students in authentic Garba form, in curated concentric circles with Mataji at the centre, was something we had never experienced before. Learning about our roots and culture through our college curriculum was both meaningful and fun.” Akshay Desai believes the devotional aspect of Garba is increasingly being overlooked. “Garba is more than dance and music. Traditionally, Mataji is placed at the centre and the celebration happens around the goddess.At many modern Garba events, that traditional touch has been lost,” he says. For Ritwisha, performing the aarti together was among the highlights. “It was my first experience of something so devotional yet fun. The authenticity was remarkable, and all 500 students performing the aarti together was truly special,” she says.Another participant, adds, “As more than 500 of us danced together, I realised Garba is more than just a dance. Despite coming from different backgrounds, we moved in synchrony as part of one celebration.”“Since the last three years, every student pursuing an undergrad course has to take a co-curricular subject like sports, theatre, yoga, classical, dance, folk dance etc and colleges like Somaiya, Mithibai, NM, Thakur have given options that include 30 hours per semester of garba and the are evaluated on it on it for academic credit. Students take structured classes to learn traditional, authentic Garba forms taught by professional garba exponents,” explains Jigar Soni, a professional garba instructor who teaches around 4000 students per year.
Article Summary: Singer Bhoomi Trivedi lifted the evening with her presence. For Jigar Soni, the senior garba instructor that was the whole point. "The young generation has to learn to celebrate garba as a festival, not an event"

Article Title: Central team starts two-day drought assessment in Marathwada
Article Text:
File photo : TOITOI

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





A central team will fan out across drought-hit pockets of Marathwada from Friday to assess the severity of the rainfall deficit, water scarcity, crop damage and fodder availability. Its findings will help determine Maharashtra ’s case for assistance from the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF).The inter-ministerial team, headed by Mukundan Agrawal, joint secretary in the Union agriculture ministry, reached Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar late on Thursday. The team will spend two days inspecting affected areas in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Jalna and Beed districts.The visit comes amid concerns over drinking water availability for the coming months, possible dependence on tankers, fodder shortages, migration and distress among farmers and agricultural workers.State govt flagged these concerns in a presentation to the central team in Mumbai on Thursday. Chief secretary Rajesh Agrawal highlighted the impact of deficient rainfall and the possibility of villages requiring tanker water in the months ahead.Officials also presented district-wise data on rainfall, crop damage, drinking-water sources and fodder availability, along with projections for the next seven months.The team will begin its ground inspection at 9 am Friday, covering Shendra and Nanegaon in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district and Kingaon Wadi, Jamkhed in Badnapur taluka and Ambad in Jalna district. Officials will brief the team on rainfall, crop conditions and water availability.The team will then head to Beed and visit drought-hit areas of Gevrai taluka, including Ardhmasla and Pargaon Japti, before halting there overnight.On Saturday, the team will visit Manjarsumba, Khandala, Vaidya Kinhi, Sonegaon and areas of Patoda taluka. It will later hold a review meeting with the Beed collector before returning to Navi Mumbai via Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.The Marathwada visit is part of a wider central assessment of Maharashtra’s drought situation. A second team is covering Ahilyanagar and Solapur, while another is inspecting Yavatmal, Washim and adjoining scarcity-hit areas of Vidarbha.

Article Title: Mumbai-bound traffic hit after hatchback catches fire on Vashi Creek bridge
Article Text:

NAVI MUMBAI: Vehicular traffic from Navi Mumbai towards Mumbai was disrupted for around 30 minutes after a hatchback caught fire while crossing the Vashi Creek Bridge on Friday at around 7.30pm.The driver escaped unhurt. He immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. However, the fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred.Vashi traffic police alerted the Vashi fire brigade, which reached the spot within 15 minutes. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.Sunil Kadam, senior inspector of the Vashi traffic unit, said the driver was identified as Sumit Bhikaji Kadam.“At around 7.45pm, we received a call from one Rahul, whose full name is not known, informing us that a car had caught fire on the Mumbai-bound lane of the Vashi Creek Bridge,” said AV Sisode, the on-duty fireman at Vashi fire station.“In the meantime, we also received a call from the Vashi traffic police and immediately rushed to the spot with a fire tender. The Mumbai fire brigade team had also reached the spot as there was some confusion over the jurisdiction,” Sisode said.The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the Vashi fire brigade team returned to the station at around 8.30pm.
